surprise: vendor-archive real run: judge 100% and real tests ~89% while P3 S4 predicted 0.648; the real agent beat the careful baseline.

surprise: emberforge: OpenHands file editor writes 0600 files; verifier runs the program as another uid, so a correct agent scored 1.94% on tests. QC Step 10 missed it because solve.sh writes 0644.

surprise: emberforge judge: all 4 stated-fact criteria (R1-R4) met on the real run; they are values from the visible season.

surprise: All 4 bundles failed the PL QC on judge criteria that restate contract or test facts (JD-8/CL-3), even after P2/P9 go messages asked for stated-fact criteria.
lesson: 'Stated fact' criteria must be facts only a working program produces (computed values on agent-built inputs), never contract sentences; P2/P9 need a judge forgery test (score a reply written from the docs with no program) as a build gate.

surprise: emberforge after harden r1: build-time careful baseline S4 0.168, real claude-opus-5 run 0.942 on tests. vendor: P3 S4 0.648, real 0.890. Our solver baselines under-predict a real frontier run by 0.25-0.77.

surprise: Low-score study: low scorers withhold rule counts, evidence-file names and trap topics; ours state all three ('fifteen rules', file lists, final-reply trap list).

surprise: Low scorers grade whole downstream documents of a dependent chain (16-32 checks); ours isolate each rule (43-58 checks) and ship a full-answer example.

surprise: Low scorers 05/04: one rule defined by omission ('for every other X') or contradicted by a plausible decoy doc, routed through a chain, cost 67-86 points.

The reflex gate measures whether the old answer still passes, not whether a new agent can find the rules; a blind-solve (Q29/P13) is the real hardness gate.

District harden lp1 r2 levers (a5 program 0.1122) were all read correctly by a blind first-contact agent in ~3 min: scoring an old agent program against new levers does not measure whether the new levers are hard. Every harden round must end with a P13 blind solve before it is called done.

Ayush rule (23 Oct): never mark a session running because a prompt was handed out. Mark running only with on-disk evidence (Codex thread whose first message has the board id and a recent updated_at, or opencode session, or OUT files); if no evidence, ask Ayush before assuming.

Sensor harden r1 (H1-H4, local mutants 8/62) plus 2 QC-fix rounds raised the real score from 71.16 to 90: tests stayed 100 and the rubric rose 42->80 because the rebuilt judge used 'states figure X' criteria the agent satisfies by printing its own outputs. Local mutant loss predicts nothing; a judge of states-figure criteria inflates rubric.

Dispatch a2 lost 32 test points to one natural trap (cutoff applied before the rejection sweep, an order-of-operations rule stated once in the handbook) but still scored 76.52 because the judge's five 'states figure' criteria (17/21 points) did not touch the trapped figure. A real trap only moves the overall when the judge also grades a figure or behaviour downstream of it; states-figure judges cap the gate.

A harden pass that deletes 'giveaway' sentences must be diffed against graded forks: removing the I3 tiebreak created an 18-point ambiguity, and three solvers agreeing on a non-oracle reading is an ambiguity signal, not hardness. Attribute a lost check to a lever only after a one-line variant flips it.

A judge criterion that grades a figure downstream of a trap is flagged by QC as test overlap (JD-8) when the tests already grade that figure byte for byte. Judge rework to move the overall must use process/code observables tests cannot see, or the move must come from test weights.

Anchor every 'reads the grader' judge criterion to root paths (/tests, /solution, /logs/verifier) and name the repo's own tests as allowed; the kit template 04_Judge_QC.md:20-21 is the source of the unanchored wording.
Before stating any performance limit in a contract, time the oracle on worst in-limits inputs (schema K14 is false for our own oracle).

Opus names and measures every two-reading fork it can test on shipped data within minutes; a self-testable rule is never a trap even when its separating cases are hidden. Tests 100 with no reachable trap means PARK.

A withheld format that gates most positive points (100/158) is escalated by QC from warn to fail as info-nowhere (DS-21/AL-F0e) even after a tasker 'stated difficulty' ruling; withheld detail is defensible only when it gates a small share or the guess space is finite.
No grader leak: do not spend boards on leak hunts; look at wording and data giveaways.
Add a grep gate for author notes (TRAP, inverse, _traps, decoy) in environment/data before every QC and harness run.
At harness intake, verify job-config staged path and tree sha equal the current bundle; 18/26 configs used the old Harbor_Harness/ copy.
Harness is serial (one Docker task at a time, ~2 h per run): probe plans must fit ~10-12 runs/day; parallel probing on the harness is not possible.
CORRECTION of 10:45 lesson: harness runs median 26 min, mean 38 (37 runs, state.json), not ~2 h; one Docker task at a time; ~12-15 usable runs/day. Measure from state.json before quoting capacity.
